example.pinyin: Zuótiān wǎnshang xiàyǔ le.
example.english: It rained last night.
example.fact: 昨 never appears alone as a stand-alone word in modern Mandarin — it only shows up bound to a time word, as in 昨天 ('yesterday') or the more literary 昨夜 ('last night'), unlike its partner 天, which functions perfectly well by itself to mean 'day' or 'sky.'

examples.pinyin: Nǐ zuótiān qù nǎr le?
examples.english: Where did you go yesterday?

examples.pinyin: Zuótiān shì wǒ de shēngrì.
examples.english: Yesterday was my birthday.

components.note: 日 (sun) — time and day, as in 时, 晚, 明: 昨 is a past day.
乍 (zhà) is a close sound clue for zuó; 乍 also in 作 zuò, 怎 zěn and 炸 zhà.
大 (big person) — a person with a line above the head, marking the sky above; tiān = heaven, sky, day.

example.pinyin: Zhèyàng zuò bù hǎo.
example.english: It's not good to do it this way.
example.fact: 不好 attached right after certain verbs takes on the idiomatic sense "hard to, difficult to" beyond plainly negating 好 ("good") — 不好说 doesn't mean "bad to say" but "hard to say," and 不好办 means a matter is "difficult to handle," a shift a literal word-by-word reading misses.

examples.pinyin: Zhège bànfǎ bù hǎo.
examples.english: This method is no good.

examples.pinyin: Tā jīntiān xīnqíng bù hǎo.
examples.english: He's in a bad mood today.

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
子 (child) — a woman with her child: the picture of something good.

example.pinyin: Tā yíxiàzi zhuāzhù le jīhuì.
example.english: He seized the opportunity in an instant.
example.fact: 住 as a verb complement marks something being secured or held fast, not just touched briefly — the same 住 turns 记 ("to note, remember") into 记住 ("commit to memory"), and 站 ("to stand") into 站住 ("stand firm, stop right there"), a small but recurring complement family built around the idea of "staying put."

examples.pinyin: Kuài zhuāzhù wǒ de shǒu!
examples.english: Quick, grab my hand!

examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá zhuāzhùle nàge xiǎotōu.
examples.english: The police caught the thief.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: to seize.
爪 (zhǎo, claw) is a close sound clue for zhuā and fits the meaning: grab with claws.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做.
主 (zhǔ) is a close sound clue for zhù; also in 注 zhù and 柱 zhù, and 主 means master (a person who stays).

example.hanzi: 请把会议内容记录下来。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ huìyì nèiróng jìlù xiàlai.
example.english: Please record the content of the meeting.
example.fact: 记录 pairs two independently "recording"-flavored characters: 记 (built from 讠 "speech" plus 己 "oneself," originally writing down one's own notes) and 录 (a pictograph of a hand tool used for carving records) — like 紧张 elsewhere in this very batch, another case of Mandarin reinforcing a meaning by doubling near-synonymous halves.

examples.hanzi: 我把电话号码记录在本子上。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ diànhuà hàomǎ jìlù zài běnzi shàng.
examples.english: I wrote the phone number down in my notebook.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì tā de zuì hǎo jìlù.
examples.english: This is his best record.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; 记 is to note down or remember.
己 (jǐ) is a close sound clue for jì; 己 also sounds out 纪 jì and 起 qǐ.
录 (lù) gives sound to 绿 lǜ, 禄 lù and 碌 lù; as a word it means to record.

example.pinyin: Qǐng zài gěi wǒ yìdiǎnr shíjiān.
example.english: Please give me a little more time.
example.fact: The 儿 in 点儿 isn't the word for 'child' — it's 'erhua,' a suffix that fuses onto a syllable as a retroflex -r sound, common in Beijing-flavored Mandarin to add a light, casual, often diminutive flavor. 点儿 and plain 点 are largely interchangeable, but the erhua form reads as noticeably more colloquial.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhǐ chīle yìdiǎnr.
examples.english: I only ate a little.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ shuō de màn diǎnr.
examples.english: Please speak a little slower.

components.note: 灬 (fire) — heat and burning, as in 热 hot, 照 shine, 黑 black; a dot is a small spot like a spark.
占 (zhàn) is a loose sound clue for diǎn; 占 also sounds out 站 zhàn and 粘 zhān.
儿 (child, legs) — shows a person's legs; in 兒 the top was a child's soft skull. As an ending (这儿) it adds the er sound; 儿 also in 先, 兄, 光.

meanings: (form of address between male friends) old chap

example.pinyin: Lǎoxiōng, hǎojiǔ bújiàn!
example.english: Buddy, long time no see!
example.fact: The 老 in 老兄 doesn't mean the person is actually old — as a prefix before a term of address (老兄, 老张, 老朋友) 老 signals familiarity and warmth rather than age, the same affectionate "老 + name/role" pattern Chinese uses for close friends of any age.

examples.pinyin: Lǎoxiōng, nǐ zài zhèr gàn shénme?
examples.english: Buddy, what are you doing here?

examples.pinyin: Lǎoxiōng, jiè wǒ yìdiǎn qián, hǎo ma?
examples.english: Pal, can you lend me a bit of money?

components.note: 耂 (old) — 老 pictures an old person with long hair leaning on a staff; the short form 耂 is also in 考 test and 孝 filial.
儿 (person, legs) — with 口 mouth on top: the elder brother who speaks for the family. 兄 also in 况 kuàng.

example.hanzi: 这些学生来自不同的国家。
example.pinyin: Zhèxiē xuésheng láizì bùtóng de guójiā.
example.english: These students come from different countries.
example.fact: 来自 sits at a more formal, written register than the everyday spoken pattern 从...来 ("come from...") — it shows up constantly in bios, news reports, and official introductions (来自中国的代表, "a representative from China"), but would sound slightly stiff in casual conversation, where 从哪儿来 is more natural.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ láizì nǎ ge guójiā?
examples.english: Which country are you from?

examples.hanzi: 这个想法来自一个小孩。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiǎngfǎ láizì yí ge xiǎohái.
examples.english: This idea came from a child.

components.note: 来 (come) — it began as a picture of a wheat plant; the sound was borrowed for "come". 麦 (wheat) still shows it, with a root 夂 added.
自 (self) — picture of a nose; Chinese speakers point to the nose to mean "I", so it became "self" (compare 鼻 bí, nose, which adds 畀).
走 (walk, run) — movement: 起, 超, 趣, 赶; 越 is to cross over, to exceed.
戉 (yuè) sounds exactly like 越.

example.pinyin: Tiān yuè lái yuè lěng le.
example.english: It's getting colder and colder.
example.fact: 越…越… is the 'the more … the more …' pattern: 越学越有意思 ('the more you study, the more interesting'). 越来越 + adjective means 'more and more'. 越 is also a verb, as in 超越 (surpass).

examples.pinyin: Wàimiàn de yǔ yuè xià yuè dà le.
examples.english: The rain outside is getting heavier and heavier.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yuè zháojí, yuè róngyì chūcuò.
examples.english: The more anxious you are, the easier it is to make mistakes.

example.hanzi: 我妹妹明年要上大学了。
example.pinyin: Wǒ mèimei míngnián yào shàng dàxué le.
example.english: My younger sister is going to start university next year.
example.fact: 学 (a roof 冖 sheltering 子 "child") shows up scaled by size rather than by grade or age band the way English does: 小学 ("small learning") is elementary school, 中学 ("middle learning") is secondary school, and 大学 ("great learning") is university — a size metaphor for increasing scope of study.

examples.pinyin: Tā zài Běijīng de dàxué dúshū.
examples.english: He studies at a university in Beijing.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ shì nǎ suǒ dàxué bìyè de?
examples.english: Which university did you graduate from?

components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
子 (child) — a child learning under a roof: the top shows hands over a house, and the child 子 below. Also gives 觉 jué its upper part.

example.hanzi: 她每天都要照顾生病的爸爸。
example.pinyin: Tā měitiān dōu yào zhàogu shēngbìng de bàba.
example.english: She has to take care of her sick father every day.
example.fact: 照 ("to shine light on, illuminate") and 顾 ("to turn one's head and look back at") combine into a caring, watchful gaze — 照顾 pictures someone keeping an attentive eye on another person, a fittingly gentle literal image behind the everyday word for "to take care of."

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào hǎohāo zhàogu zìjǐ.
examples.english: You should take good care of yourself.

examples.pinyin: Xièxie nǐ zhàogu wǒ de háizi.
examples.english: Thank you for looking after my child.

components.note: 灬 (fire) — fire and heat, as in 热 hot, 点 dot, 黑 black: light shining.
昭 (zhāo) is a close sound clue for zhào; 昭 itself means bright.
页 (head) — heads and faces, as in 头, 题, 顶: to turn the head and look.
厄 stands in for 雇 (gù) in the traditional 顧; the clue is only loose today.

example.pinyin: Wáng tàitai, hǎojiǔ bújiàn!
example.english: Mrs. Wang, long time no see!
example.fact: 太太 sits at the polite, formal end of a spectrum of words for "wife": 妻子 is the neutral, written-register term, 老婆 is the casual, affectionate one, and 太太 (also doubling as the polite title "Mrs.") is what you'd use to address or refer respectfully to someone else's wife, like 王太太 for "Mrs. Wang."

examples.pinyin: Tàitai zài chúfáng zuòfàn.
examples.english: My wife is cooking in the kitchen.

examples.pinyin: Lǐ tàitai shì wǒmen de línjū.
examples.english: Mrs. Li is our neighbor.

components.note: 大 (big) — an extra stroke below emphasises it: bigger than big, too much. 太 also sounds out 泰 tài.
大 (big) — an extra stroke below emphasises it: bigger than big, too much. 太 also sounds out 泰 tài.

example.pinyin: Zhè zhī gǒu fēicháng cōngming.
example.english: This dog is very clever.
example.fact: 聪 traces back to 耳 ("ear"), since sharp hearing was seen as a marker of mental acuity, while 明 pictures the combined brightness of 日 ("sun") and 月 ("moon") — 聪明 literally reads as "sharp of ear, bright as sun-and-moon," pairing acute perception with brilliance into the everyday word for "smart, clever."

examples.pinyin: Tā de háizi hěn cōngming.
examples.english: Her child is very smart.

examples.pinyin: Zhège bànfǎ zhēn cōngming.
examples.english: This is a really clever solution.

components.note: 耳 (ear) — hearing, as in 听, 闻, 联: sharp ears, then quick-witted.
总 (zǒng) is a close sound clue for cōng; also in 葱 cōng.
日 (sun) — the sun beside the moon: two light sources, so bright and clear.
月 (moon) — as in 朋, 期, 有; here it brightens the night.

example.hanzi: 我本来想去旅行,但是没有时间。
example.pinyin: Wǒ běnlái xiǎng qù lǚxíng, dànshì méiyǒu shíjiān.
example.english: I originally wanted to travel, but I didn't have time.
example.fact: 本来 almost always sets up an implicit contrast with what actually happened — "originally/at first X, but then Y" — even when 但是 or 结果 isn't spoken aloud, a listener expects the sentence to pivot away from the original plan, similar to how English "originally" implies a plan that changed.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ běnlái bù xiǎng qù de.
examples.english: I didn't want to go at first.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì tā běnlái de yàngzi.
examples.english: This is how he originally looked.

components.note: 木 (tree) — a tree with a mark at the base: the root, hence source, origin, and the measure word for books.
来 (come) — it began as a picture of a wheat plant; the sound was borrowed for "come". 麦 (wheat) still shows it, with a root 夂 added.

example.hanzi: 大家一起为运动员加油!
example.pinyin: Dàjiā yìqǐ wèi yùndòngyuán jiāyóu!
example.english: Everyone cheer for the athletes together!
example.fact: 加油 literally means "to add oil/fuel" (as at a gas station) but has become one of Mandarin's most common cheering exclamations — shouted alone as 加油! ("go for it! you've got this!") at sports events, exams, and any moment someone needs encouragement, extending the fueling image to a boost of effort.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yídìng néng yíng, jiāyóu!
examples.english: You can definitely win, keep going!

examples.hanzi: 车没油了,我们去加油吧。
examples.pinyin: Chē méi yóu le, wǒmen qù jiāyóu ba.
examples.english: The car is out of gas, let's go fill up.

components.note: 力 (strength) — with 口 mouth: adding strength by words, hence to add, to increase. 加 also in 架 jià and 驾 jià.
氵 (water radical, 三点水) — marks liquids and things that flow, as in 河 river, 汤 soup, 酒 liquor; here an oily liquid.
由 (yóu) sounds exactly like 油 — the same sound clue appears in 邮 yóu and 柚 yòu.

example.hanzi: 实际上,这个计划根本不可行。
example.pinyin: Shíjìshàng, zhège jìhuà gēnběn bù kěxíng.
example.english: In fact, this plan isn't feasible at all.
example.fact: 上 here works as an abstract locative suffix meaning roughly "on the level/plane of" rather than physical "on top of" — the same pattern shows up in 基本上 ("basically," literally "on the basic level") and 理论上 ("theoretically," "on the theoretical level"), a recurring way Mandarin turns a noun into "from the X standpoint."

examples.hanzi: 实际上,我从来没去过那里。
examples.pinyin: Shíjì shàng, wǒ cónglái méi qùguo nàlǐ.
examples.english: In fact, I've never been there.

examples.hanzi: 他看起来很年轻,实际上已经五十岁了。
examples.pinyin: Tā kàn qǐlai hěn niánqīng, shíjì shàng yǐjīng wǔshí suì le.
examples.english: He looks young, but is actually fifty.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 字, 室: a house stocked with goods, so solid and real.
阝 (mound, left-side form of 阜 hill) — relates to hills, walls and places, as in 院 courtyard, 阳 sun-side, 陆 land; fits 际 as a boundary.
示 (shì) is only a loose sound hint — traditional 際 used 祭 (jì), and simplification swapped in 示.
上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.
甘 (sweet) — marks sweetness, as in 甘 itself and 某; 甜 pairs it with 舌 tongue: sweet to the tongue.
舌 (tongue) — the organ that tastes, as in 话 and 活.

example.pinyin: Zhège píngguǒ hěn tián.
example.english: This apple is very sweet.
example.fact: 甜 means sweet to the taste and can describe a person's voice or smile: 声音很甜, 甜蜜 (sweet, happy). 甜 is the opposite of 苦 (kǔ, bitter) and 酸.

examples.hanzi: 她笑得很甜，大家都喜欢她。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiào de hěn tián, dàjiā dōu xǐhuan tā.
examples.english: She smiles sweetly, and everyone likes her.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bú ài chī tài tián de dōngxi.
examples.english: I don't like eating things that are too sweet.

components.note: 忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 快, 忙, 情: fear is a feeling.
白 (bái) is a close sound clue for pà; 白 also in 拍 pāi and 伯 bó.

example.pinyin: Wǒ pà hēi.
example.english: I'm afraid of the dark.
example.fact: 怕 can take a noun (怕狗) or a clause (怕他不来), and in speech it can also mean 'I'm afraid that…', as in 恐怕. It's more everyday than 害怕, which often takes no object.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ bié pà, wǒ zài zhèlǐ.
examples.english: Don't be afraid, I'm here.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ pà lěng, suǒyǐ duō chuān yīfu.
examples.english: I'm afraid of the cold, so I wear more clothes.

example.pinyin: Nǐ zài zhèlǐ zhù le duōjiǔ?
example.english: How long have you lived here?
example.fact: 多久 belongs to a whole family of "多 + adjective" questions asking for a measurement — 多大 ("how old/big"), 多高 ("how tall"), 多久 ("how long, of time") — the same productive pattern that lets 多 turn almost any scalar adjective into its corresponding question word.

examples.pinyin: Zhège diànyǐng yǒu duō jiǔ?
examples.english: How long is this movie?

examples.pinyin: Nǐ xué Zhōngwén xuéle duōjiǔ?
examples.english: How long have you been learning Chinese?

components.note: 多 (many) — two 夕 stacked, repeated again and again: so "many, much, more".
勹 (wrap) — the visible part, a bent shape. Memory aid: a stooped figure under weight, wearing down over time — a long time, as in 好久.
灸 (jiǔ, moxibustion) — 久 is its sound part, same sound jiǔ. Another is 玖 jiǔ. The old picture of 久 is disputed.

example.hanzi: 他工作努力,并且十分负责。
example.pinyin: Tā gōngzuò nǔlì, bìngqiě shífēn fùzé.
example.english: He works hard and is also very responsible.
example.fact: 并且 sits at a more formal, written register than its everyday synonym 而且 — both mean "moreover, and," but 并且 shows up far more in reports, contracts, and formal writing, while 而且 dominates ordinary conversation, a register distinction the English gloss doesn't capture.

examples.hanzi: 她会唱歌,并且唱得很好听。
examples.pinyin: Tā huì chànggē, bìngqiě chàng de hěn hǎotīng.
examples.english: She can sing, and sings beautifully.

examples.hanzi: 这家店很便宜,并且很干净。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn hěn piányi, bìngqiě hěn gānjìng.
examples.english: This shop is cheap and also clean.

components.note: 并 (combine) — simplified from 並, which showed two figures standing side by side; hence together, also, and (并且).
且 (moreover) — an old picture of an offering stand or ancestral tablet. As a sound clue it gives 祖 zǔ, 组 zǔ, 租 zū and 助 zhù.

meanings: direct (opposite: indirect 間接|间接[jian4 jie1])

example.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ zhíjiē liánxì wǒ.
example.english: You can contact me directly.
example.fact: 直 ("straight," pictured as an eye 目 looking fixedly ahead) plus 接 ("to connect") combine transparently into "a straight connection" — giving 直接 its modern sense "direct, immediate," whether describing a flight with no layovers or a blunt, straightforward way of speaking.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ zhíjiē gàosu tā.
examples.english: You can tell him directly.

examples.hanzi: 这趟飞机是直接到上海的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tàng fēijī shì zhíjiē dào Shànghǎi de.
examples.english: This flight goes directly to Shanghai.

components.note: 目 (eye) — sighting along a straight line. 直 also sounds out 值 zhí and 植 zhí.
扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: receiving something by hand.
妾 (qiè) is only a loose sound clue for jiē.

example.hanzi: 对于这个问题,大家意见不一。
example.pinyin: Duìyú zhège wèntí, dàjiā yìjiàn bùyī.
example.english: Regarding this issue, people have different opinions.
example.fact: 对于 and its near-synonym 关于 both translate as "about, regarding," but they lean differently: 对于 usually introduces something people react to or take a stance on, while 关于 more neutrally names a topic of discussion (关于这个问题的报告, "a report about this issue") — a nuance easy to miss when both get flattened to "about" in English.

examples.hanzi: 对于学生来说,时间很宝贵。
examples.pinyin: Duìyú xuésheng lái shuō, shíjiān hěn bǎoguì.
examples.english: For students, time is precious.

examples.pinyin: Tā duìyú zhè jiàn shì hěn guānxīn.
examples.english: He cares a lot about this matter.

components.note: 寸 (hand, inch) — hands and measuring, as in 寻 seek, 导 lead, 射 shoot; 对 faces someone or matches a pair. 又 here only stands in for the left side of 對.
于 (yú) is a sound clue for 宇 yǔ and 芋 yù; it is a light grammar word meaning "at, to".
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; 记 is to note down or remember.
己 (jǐ) is a close sound clue for jì; 己 also sounds out 纪 jì and 起 qǐ.

example.pinyin: Wǒ jì bu zhù tā de míngzi.
example.english: I can't remember his name.
example.fact: 记 is used in 记得 (remember), 记住 (commit to memory), 日记 (diary) and 记者 (reporter). 记得 and 记住 differ: 记得 describes a state, 记住 describes the effort.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng jìzhù wǒ de diànhuà ma?
examples.english: Can you remember my phone number?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān dōu xiě rìjì.
examples.english: I write a diary every day.

example.pinyin: Tiānqì tūrán biànlěng le.
example.english: The weather suddenly turned cold.
example.fact: 突 pictures a dog (犬) bursting suddenly out of its den (穴) — a vivid, almost cinematic image of something unexpected breaking loose — which 突然 then generalizes into the everyday adverb for anything happening "suddenly, abruptly."

examples.pinyin: Tā tūrán zhànle qǐlai.
examples.english: He suddenly stood up.

examples.pinyin: Tūrán, dēng miè le.
examples.english: Suddenly, the lights went out.

components.note: 穴 (cave, hole) — the radical of holes and hollow spaces, as in 空 empty, 窗 window, 穿 pierce.
犬 (dog) — a dog bursting out of its den 穴: the picture of something sudden and unexpected.
灬 (fire) — heat and burning, as in 热 hot, 点 dot, 照 shine. 然 first meant "to burn" (燃 rán adds 火 later); "so, naturally" is borrowed.
肰 (rán) gives the exact sound and shows up in 燃 rán.
口 (mouth) — marks speech, sounds and eating, as in 叫 call, 吃 eat, 唱 sing; 啥 is the colloquial what, as in 干啥 doing what.
舍 (shè) — close sound: 啥 shá.

example.pinyin: Nǐ shuō shá?
example.english: What did you say?
example.fact: 啥 is a colloquial northern way to say 什么, common in Northeastern dialect and sitcoms: 干啥 ('what are you doing?'), 啥事 ('what's up?'). In formal writing, avoid it.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ wǎnfàn xiǎng chī diǎn shá?
examples.english: What do you want to eat for dinner?

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì shá yìsi ya?
examples.english: What does this mean?

example.pinyin: Jǐngchá duìzhe lúntāi kāiqiāng le.
example.english: The police fired at the tire.
example.fact: 开 here means neither "to open" nor even its more familiar "to start/operate" sense in isolation — 开枪 belongs to a wide family of 开 + noun collocations for activating something (开车 "to drive," literally "operate a car"; 开灯 "to turn on a light," literally "open a light"), with "firing a gun" folded into the same pattern as flipping a switch.

examples.pinyin: Lièrén duìzhe tiānkōng kāiqiāng le.
examples.english: The hunter fired his gun at the sky.

examples.pinyin: Diànyǐng lǐ, jǐngchá méiyǒu kāiqiāng.
examples.english: In the movie, the police did not fire.

components.note: 廾 (two hands) — in 開 two hands lift the bar of a gate; 开 is the simplified shape. Compare 关 (close).
木 (wood) — 枪 first meant a wooden spear; wood radical also in 棍 stick and 板 board.
仓 (cāng) hints at the sound — close to qiāng; the same part is in 抢 qiǎng and 苍 cāng.
聲 (traditional) — a hanging stone chime struck, with 耳 (ear) below: a sound you hear. 声 keeps only the top, so the picture is mostly lost.
士 (scholar) — the top of 声 is only a leftover of the old chime, not 'scholar'. Do not read meaning into it.

example.pinyin: Wǒ tīngdàole yí gè shēngyīn.
example.english: I heard a sound.
example.fact: 声 is the sound or voice: 声音, 大声 (loudly), 小声 (quietly) and 声调 (tone). It's also the measure word for calls and sounds: 叫了一声 ('called once').

examples.pinyin: Qǐng xiǎoshēng yìdiǎnr.
examples.english: Please keep your voice down.

examples.pinyin: Wàimiàn yǒu hěn dà de shēngyīn.
examples.english: There is a loud noise outside.

example.hanzi: 除非你道歉,否则我不会原谅你。
example.pinyin: Chúfēi nǐ dàoqiàn, fǒuzé wǒ bú huì yuánliàng nǐ.
example.english: Unless you apologize, I won't forgive you.
example.fact: 除非 commonly pairs with 否则 or 不然 ("otherwise") in the fixed frame "除非 X, 否则 Y" ("unless X, otherwise Y") — the same paired-conjunction habit behind 因为...所以... elsewhere in this deck, where Mandarin keeps both halves of a logical relationship spoken explicitly rather than dropping one as redundant.

examples.hanzi: 除非下雨,我们明天都去。
examples.pinyin: Chúfēi xiàyǔ, wǒmen míngtiān dōu qù.
examples.english: Unless it rains, we'll go tomorrow.

examples.pinyin: Chúfēi nǐ lái, fǒuzé wǒ bú qù.
examples.english: Unless you come, I won't go.

components.note: 阝 on the left is 阜 (steps, hill) — as in 院, 阳, 阴: 除 first meant palace steps; to step away, remove.
余 (yú) is a loose sound clue for chú; 余 also in 涂 tú, 途 tú and 徐 xú.
非 (not) — two wings spread in opposite directions, so "opposed, not". Gives sound to 啡 fēi, 排 pái and 悲 bēi.
隹 (short-tailed bird) — birds: 难, 雀, 雄; 集 is birds 隹 gathered on a tree 木: to gather.

example.pinyin: Zhè bù diànshìjù yǒu sānshí jí.
example.english: This TV drama has thirty episodes.
example.fact: 集 is a measure word for TV episodes (第一集) and a verb meaning 'to gather': 集合 (assemble), 集中 (concentrate), 收集 (collect). It also means a market in 赶集 (go to a market fair).

examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànshìjù yǒu èrshí jí.
examples.english: This TV series has twenty episodes.

examples.pinyin: Dàjiā bā diǎn zài ménkǒu jíhé.
examples.english: Everyone gathers at the door at eight.

components.note: 广 (building, shelter) — houses and shops: 床, 库, 座; 店 is a shop.
占 (zhàn) is a loose sound hint; same part in 站 zhàn and 战 zhàn.

example.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn hěn yǒumíng.
example.english: This shop is very famous.
example.fact: 店 is a shop, with the measure word 家 (一家店). Common compounds are 商店 (shop), 书店 (bookstore), 饭店 (restaurant or hotel) and 酒店 (hotel).

examples.pinyin: Fùjìn yǒu yì jiā kāfēidiàn.
examples.english: There is a coffee shop nearby.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn jǐ diǎn guānmén?
examples.english: What time does this shop close?

components.note: 酉 (wine jar) — marks liquor and fermentation, as in 酒 liquor, 醉 drunk, 醒 sober; 酷 is strong, then harsh and cool.
告 (gào) is a loose hint for kù; 靠 kào and 浩 hào share it.

example.pinyin: Zhège yóuxì tài kù le!
example.english: This game is so cool!
example.fact: 酷 originally meant 'cruel' (残酷) and 'strong' (of liquor), and today it also means 'cool', borrowed from English as a sound match. The two senses sit side by side: 酷刑 (torture) and 很酷 (very cool).

examples.pinyin: Tā de xīn shǒujī zhēn kù!
examples.english: His new phone is so cool!

examples.pinyin: Zhège zàoxíng tài kù le.
examples.english: This look is so cool.

components.note: 止 (foot) — a foot heading straight for a target line: upright, correct. 正 gives sound to 证 zhèng, 整 zhěng and 政 zhèng.
巾 (cloth) — cloth and clothing, as in 布 cloth, 带 belt, 帽 hat; 常 first meant a long skirt (裳 cháng).
尚 (shàng) is a loose sound clue for cháng; 尚 also sounds out 堂 táng and 掌 zhǎng.

example.hanzi: 医生说检查结果都很正常。
example.pinyin: Yīshēng shuō jiǎnchá jiéguǒ dōu hěn zhèngcháng.
example.english: The doctor said the checkup results are all normal.
example.fact: 正常 literally combines 正 ("correct, upright") and 常 ("usual, constant") — something that is both "correct" and "usual" is, quite transparently, "normal."

examples.pinyin: Tā de tǐwēn hěn zhèngcháng.
examples.english: His body temperature is normal.

examples.pinyin: Huǒchē zhèngcháng yùnxíng.
examples.english: The trains are running normally.

components.note: 歹 (bad bone) — death and decay, as in 残 remnant, 烈 fierce, 殊 special.
匕 (person) — a person beside bones: death.
亡 (die, lose) — dictionary: a man in a coffin; early forms may be a person hiding or fleeing. Treat as a memory aid. It also gives sound clues in 忙 máng, 盲 máng.
亠 (lid) — the top. Memory aid: a lid closed over a person — gone, dead, as in 死亡.

example.hanzi: 这场车祸造成了三人死亡。
example.pinyin: Zhè chǎng chēhuò zàochéng le sān rén sǐwáng.
example.english: This car accident caused three deaths.
example.fact: 死亡 is the neutral, clinical register for "death" used in news reports and statistics — in everyday conversation about a person’s passing, Chinese speakers usually reach instead for the softer, more respectful 去世 or 过世, since a bare 死 (or 死亡 applied to someone you know) can sound abrupt or even callous.

examples.hanzi: 他的死亡让大家很难过。
examples.pinyin: Tā de sǐwáng ràng dàjiā hěn nánguò.
examples.english: His death made everyone sad.

examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng bìng de sǐwánglǜ hěn dī.
examples.english: The death rate of this disease is very low.

components.note: 纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord words: 红 red, 给 give, 线 line; a thread has an end, which fits 终 end.
冬 (dōng) rhymes with 终 zhōng, and 冬 originally meant the end (of the year) too — so it helps sound and sense.
于 (yú) is a sound clue for 宇 yǔ and 芋 yù; it is a light grammar word meaning "at, to".

example.hanzi: 经过八个小时的飞行,我们终于到了。
example.pinyin: Jīngguò bā gè xiǎoshí de fēixíng, wǒmen zhōngyú dào le.
example.english: After an eight-hour flight, we finally arrived.
example.fact: 终于 marks the end of a long wait or difficult process and usually carries a note of relief or emotional payoff — its more neutral cousin 最后 ("lastly, in the end") simply marks sequence, with no implication that the wait was hard-won.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhōngyú zhǎodàole gōngzuò.
examples.english: I finally found a job.

examples.pinyin: Yǔ zhōngyú tíng le.
examples.english: The rain finally stopped.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions done by hand, as in 打 hit, 抱 hug, 拉 pull; fits 拥 to embrace or hold.
用 (yòng) is only a loose sound hint for yōng — same ending -ong.
月 (flesh/meat, not moon here) — oldest form is a hand holding a piece of meat, "to possess"; 月 as meat also appears in 肉 words like 肚 belly and 脑 brain.

example.hanzi: 她拥有十年的教学经验。
example.pinyin: Tā yōngyǒu shí nián de jiàoxué jīngyàn.
example.english: She has ten years of teaching experience.
example.fact: 拥有 is the more formal, "weightier" word for "to have" — reserved for significant or abstract possessions like wealth, rights, talent, or experience — while everyday, concrete belongings ("I have a pen") almost always just take the plain verb 有.

examples.pinyin: Tā yōngyǒu yì jiā xiǎo gōngsī.
examples.english: He owns a small company.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yōngyǒu tóngyàng de mèngxiǎng.
examples.english: We share the same dream.

components.note: 言 (speech) — written 讠 on the left of other characters: a warning is spoken.
敬 (jìng, respect) is a close sound clue for jǐng.

example.pinyin: Tā jiàole jǐngchá.
example.english: He called the police.
example.fact: 警 forms 警察 (police), 报警 (call the police) and 警告 (warning). 警察 is the person, while 警 alone is the shorter spoken form for 'police' only in compounds like 警车.

examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá zài lùkǒu zhǐhuī jiāotōng.
examples.english: The police officer is directing traffic at the intersection.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ mǎshàng bàojǐng.
examples.english: Please call the police right away.

components.note: 舟 (boat) — 舟 is the boat radical, as in 般, 航, 舰; 船 is a ship.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen zuò chuán qù nàge dǎo.
example.english: We take a boat to that island.
example.fact: 船 takes the measure word 条 for small boats and 艘 for ships, and 坐船 is the verb phrase 'to travel by boat'. Compounds include 轮船 (steamship), 飞船 (spaceship) and 船长 (captain).

examples.pinyin: Hé lǐ yǒu yì tiáo xiǎochuán.
examples.english: There is a small boat on the river.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ dì yī cì zuò dà lúnchuán.
examples.english: It's my first time taking a big ship.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 付 is handing 寸 something to a person.
付 (fù) is also the sound in 附 fù, 府 fǔ, 符 fú and 腐 fǔ.

example.pinyin: Wǒ lái fù qián.
example.english: I'll pay.
example.fact: 付 means to pay and is used in 付款 (payment), 付钱, 支付 (pay) and 付出 (devote). When paying a bill, 买单 is the casual way and 结账 is the other common phrase.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ yòng shǒujī fùkuǎn.
examples.english: You can pay with your phone.

examples.pinyin: Ràng wǒ lái fù qián, nǐ bié kèqi.
examples.english: Let me pay, don't be polite.

components.note: 氵 (water radical) — 派 first meant a stream branching off a river, which grew into branch, faction and to send out.
寸 (hand, inch) — hands and measuring, as in 寻 seek, 导 lead, 射 shoot; 对 faces someone or matches a pair. 又 here only stands in for the left side of 對.

example.hanzi: 我们周末要开一个派对。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zhōumò yào kāi yí gè pàiduì.
example.english: We're having a party this weekend.
example.fact: 派对 is a phonetic loanword transliterating English "party" — one of a small class of borrowed sound-alike words in Mandarin (alongside 咖啡 kāfēi "coffee") that carry no meaning from their individual characters, only borrowed sound.

examples.hanzi: 你来参加我的生日派对吗?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ lái cānjiā wǒ de shēngrì pàiduì ma?
examples.english: Are you coming to my birthday party?

examples.pinyin: Zuówǎn de pàiduì hěn rènao.
examples.english: Last night's party was lively.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之) — marks movement and roads, as in 过 pass, 进 enter; 遍 is going all over, then times, as in 看一遍.
扁 (biǎn) — close sound: 遍 biàn. 扁 also sounds out 编 biān and 偏 piān.

example.pinyin: Qǐng zài shuō yí biàn.
example.english: Please say it one more time.
example.fact: 遍 is a measure word for repeating a whole action from start to finish: 说一遍, 看一遍. It differs from 次 (cì), which counts any occurrence. 遍 also means 'everywhere', as in 遍地 and 走遍.

examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū wǒ kànle sān biàn.
examples.english: I've read this book three times.

examples.pinyin: Tā pǎobiànle zhěnggè chéngshì.
examples.english: She ran all over the city.

components.note: 止 (foot) — two footprints, one above the other, make a step; the same 止 is in 走 walk and 跑 run.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen qù sànbù ba.
example.english: Let's go for a walk.
example.fact: 步 is a step in a literal and abstract sense: 步行 (walk), 进步 (progress), 一步一步 (step by step) and 第一步 (first step). 散步 is 'to take a stroll'.

examples.pinyin: Tā yí bù yí bù de zǒushàng lóu.
examples.english: He walked up the stairs step by step.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen měitiān wǎnshang sànbù.
examples.english: We take a walk every evening.

components.note: 一 (line) — dictionary reads 不 as a bird flying up toward the sky 一. The meaning 'not' is a borrowing, so the shape does not explain it today.
杯 (bēi) — a character that uses 不 as a loose sound clue (木 + 不). The sound is a hint only: 不 bù vs bēi.
冉 (rǎn) — the main part. The dictionary story is two fish on a line 一: a second catch, so 'again'. It is a memory aid; the origin is unclear.
一 (one) — the top bar. Memory aid: 'one more' line on top — 再见 see you again, 再次 once more.

example.pinyin: Tā bú zài xiāngxìn tā le.
example.english: He no longer believes her.
example.fact: 不再 always sits directly before the verb to negate an ongoing or future continuation ("no longer doing X") and is regularly closed off with a sentence-final 了 to mark the change of state — its cousin 没再 instead negates a repeated action that simply didn’t happen again in the past.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen bú zài shì péngyou le.
examples.english: We are no longer friends.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bú zài chōuyān le.
examples.english: I don't smoke anymore.

components.note: 鬼 (ghost) — a creature with a big head and a hollow body. As a radical it brings in spirits: 魂 soul, 魔 demon, 愧 ashamed.

example.pinyin: Xiǎohái pà guǐ.
example.english: Kids are afraid of ghosts.
example.fact: 鬼 is a ghost and also a suffix for people with a bad habit: 酒鬼 (drunkard), 懒鬼 (lazy bones) and 小鬼 (little rascal, affectionate). 鬼 also appears in 鬼节 (Ghost Festival, in the seventh lunar month).

examples.pinyin: Zhège guǐ gùshi hěn xiàrén.
examples.english: This ghost story is scary.

examples.pinyin: Tā shì ge xiǎo táoqìguǐ.
examples.english: He is a little rascal.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — often added to characters that only imitate foreign sounds, as in 啡 and 吗.
加 (jiā) gives a rough sound for kā — 咖 only imitates the sound of "coffee" and has no meaning of its own.
口 (mouth) — marks a character used for a drinkable or spoken sound; here it only helps spell "coffee" (咖啡).
非 (fēi) sounds exactly like 啡; the same clue is in 菲 fēi and 匪 fěi.

example.hanzi: 我每天早上都喝一杯咖啡。
example.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān zǎoshang dōu hē yì bēi kāfēi.
example.english: I drink a cup of coffee every morning.
example.fact: Like 派对, 咖啡 is a sound-borrowed loanword for "coffee" — both syllables were chosen purely to approximate the foreign sound, which is why 咖 and 啡 are found in almost no other common words, existing mainly to spell out this one borrowed term.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎng hē kāfēi háishi chá?
examples.english: Would you like coffee or tea?

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā kāfēidiàn hěn ānjìng.
examples.english: This coffee shop is very quiet.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 傻 is a foolish person.

example.pinyin: Nǐ bié shǎ le.
example.english: Don't be silly.
example.fact: 傻 is 'silly' in a mild and sometimes affectionate way: 傻瓜 (fool), 装傻 (play dumb), 傻笑 (laugh foolishly). It's softer than 笨 (bèn, dull, slow-witted).

examples.hanzi: 别傻了，那不是真的，是电影。
examples.pinyin: Bié shǎ le, nà bú shì zhēn de, shì diànyǐng.
examples.english: Don't be silly, that isn't real, it's a movie.

examples.pinyin: Tā shǎshǎ de zhàn zài nàr.
examples.english: He stood there blankly.

components.note: 阝 (mound, left-side form of 阜 hill) — a hill is an obstacle, which fits 阻 to block; compare 院 courtyard, 陆 land.
且 (qiě) gives only a loose hint, but 阻 sounds exactly like 祖 zǔ and 组 zǔ, which share the same 且 part.
止 (stop) — a picture of a foot planted on the ground: where the foot stops. Seen in 步 step (two feet) and 正 correct.

example.hanzi: 警察及时阻止了这场冲突。
example.pinyin: Jǐngchá jíshí zǔzhǐ le zhè chǎng chōngtū.
example.english: The police stopped the conflict in time.
example.fact: 阻 (a hill blocking the way) and 止 (a stopped foot) both independently mean "to block, to stop" — 阻止 stacks two already near-synonymous roots into one reinforced verb, a common Chinese word-building strategy also seen in this deck’s 喜欢 and 应该.

examples.pinyin: Méiyǒu rén néng zǔzhǐ tā.
examples.english: No one can stop him.

examples.pinyin: Dàyǔ zǔzhǐle wǒmen chūmén.
examples.english: The heavy rain kept us from going out.

components.note: 心 (heart) — thought and feelings, as in 思, 感, 急: to think of someone.
相 (xiāng) is a close sound clue for xiǎng; 相 also in 箱 xiāng and 湘 xiāng.
象 (elephant) — a picture of an elephant with trunk on top and legs below. 像 likeness adds 亻; 想象 imagine, 印象 impression use the "image" sense.

example.hanzi: 很难想象没有手机的生活。
example.pinyin: Hěn nán xiǎngxiàng méiyǒu shǒujī de shēnghuó.
example.english: It's hard to imagine life without a phone.
example.fact: 想象 is the standard mainland spelling for "to imagine" — don’t be thrown by the near-identical variant 想像, still seen in some Taiwan and Hong Kong publications, which swaps in 像 ("to resemble") for 象; both point to the same word, just standardized differently by region.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng xiǎngxiàng zhège huàmiàn ma?
examples.english: Can you imagine this scene?

examples.pinyin: Háizi de xiǎngxiànglì hěn fēngfù.
examples.english: Children have rich imaginations.

components.note: 冫 (ice, 两点水) — cold and freezing: 冰 ice, 冻 freeze, 凉 cool; here simply cold.
令 (lìng) is a loose sound clue (l- start); it also sounds out 领 lǐng and 铃 líng.
青 (qīng) hints at the -ing rhyme; same part in 清 请 情 晴 精. The 争 (contend) half is not a reliable clue.

example.hanzi: 遇到问题的时候,你要保持冷静。
example.pinyin: Yùdào wèntí de shíhou, nǐ yào bǎochí lěngjìng.
example.english: When you run into a problem, you need to stay calm.
example.fact: 冷 ("cold") plus 静 ("still, quiet") combine almost literally into "cold and still" — an emotional-temperature metaphor much like English "keep a cool head," just built from the character level up rather than as a fixed idiom.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiān lěngjìng yíxià.
examples.english: Calm down first.

examples.pinyin: Tā shì ge hěn lěngjìng de rén.
examples.english: He's a very calm person.

components.note: 方 (square, direction) — early picture is disputed (a plough-like tool or lashed boats). Sound clue in 房 fáng, 防 fáng, 访 fǎng, 放 fàng.
亠 (lid) — the top. Memory aid: a lid over a bent shape — a square-cornered 'side' or place, as in 地方, 方法.
氵 (water) — water, as in 河, 海, 清: in the old form 灋, water stood for fairness, so law and method.

example.hanzi: 这是解决问题的好方法。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì jiějué wèntí de hǎo fāngfǎ.
example.english: This is a good way to solve the problem.
example.fact: 方法 names a concrete technique or procedure for getting something done, distinct from its near-synonym 办法 which leans toward a solution or workaround for a specific problem — "有办法" ("I’ve got a way") is common and casual in speech, but "有方法" sounds noticeably stiffer.

examples.pinyin: Xué wàiyǔ yǒu shénme hǎo fāngfǎ?
examples.english: What's a good way to learn a foreign language?

examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng fāngfǎ tài màn le.
examples.english: This method is too slow.

components.note: 犭 (beast, form of 犬 dog) — animals: 狗 dog, 猫 cat, 狼 wolf; 犯 is to attack or violate, hence offend.

example.pinyin: Tā fànle yí gè cuòwù.
example.english: He made a mistake.
example.fact: 犯 means to commit or to violate: 犯错 (make a mistake), 犯法 (break the law) and 犯人 (criminal). It also appears in 犯困 (feel sleepy), a colloquial phrase.

examples.pinyin: Tā fànle yí ge xiǎo cuòwù.
examples.english: He made a small mistake.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ chīle wǔfàn yòu fàn kùn le.
examples.english: After lunch I'm feeling sleepy again.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 打, 拉, 提; 扔 is to throw.
乃 (nǎi) is only a loose sound hint for rēng.

example.pinyin: Bié luàn rēng lājī.
example.english: Don't throw rubbish around.
example.fact: 扔 is the colloquial 'throw' and 'throw away': 扔掉 (throw out) and 扔球 (throw a ball). It is more casual than 丢 and 投.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ lājī rēngjìn lājītǒng.
examples.english: Please throw the trash into the bin.

examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ qiú rēng gěile wǒ.
examples.english: He threw the ball to me.
